description: A handler the platform runs per event, billed per invocation and duration, with no server for you to manage.
A message emitted by a managed service, such as S3 on object creation, that triggers work asynchronously.

The platform polls a queue such as SQS, invokes the function with a batch and deletes the batch when the invocation succeeds; a failed invocation returns the whole batch unless the function reports which messages failed.
The extra latency of creating a new execution environment: loading the code, starting the runtime and running initialization.
The cap on simultaneous executions; reserving or capping it per function protects fragile dependencies and other functions.
A handler that leaves the same result when an at-least-once event is delivered twice, often via a conditional write on an idempotency key.
